newsitem.title: USA: MCI, AT&T decline comment on Telefonica.
newsitem.headline: MCI, AT&T decline comment on Telefonica.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp on Thursday declined comment on reports that Telefonica de Espana SA was poised to choose it as a partner and possibly break with its current international partnership Unisource.
Unisource is a loose alliance made up of AT&T Corp, Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV, Telia of Sweden and Swiss Telecom.
AT&T declined to comment, and a spokeswoman said she was unable to verify if the terms of the Unisource deal precluded Telefonica from setting alliances with AT&T's rivals.

Telefonica said three weeks ago that it had talked with AT&T, MCI and MCI's merger partner British Telecommunications Plc as well as SBC Communications Inc about finding a partner that would give it a handhold in the U.S.
Analysts say that Telefonica would not only gain global scale by such a move, but would be able to exploit its brand name amongst Spanish-speaking minorities in the U.S.
They say Telefonica's Latin American interests are key assets, which generated most of the $2.4 billion of revenues that TISA, Telefonica's international unit, made last year.

The Latin American angle is thought to be why Telefonica spoke to SBC. The Texas-based regional Bell, which recently completed its acquisition of fellow-Bell Pacific Telesis Group, owns a stake in Mexico's Telefonos de Mexico.

An SBC spokesman said he was unaware of any talks with Telefonica, but noted that a focus on international operations was a major goal of SBC's merger with Pacific Telesis. (( --Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
